newsitem.title: USA: Seagate reports rise in first quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Seagate reports rise in first quarter profit.

text.p: Seagate Technology Inc. Thursday reported a better-than-expected 7.5 percent rise in fiscal first quarter profits as the computer disk drive maker reduced expenses.

Seagate, the biggest maker of devices that store information in computers, said profits for the quarter ended Sept. 27 rose to $129.4 million, or $1.06 a share, compared with net income of $120.8 million, or $1.05, in last year's third quarter. Without a $2.8 million charge for the acquisition of Sytron Corp., Seagate's earnings per share would have been $1.07.
Wall Street had expected Seagate, based in Scotts Valley, Calif., to earn $1.00 a share, based on a recent survey of 10 analysts by First Call.
First-quarter revenue dropped to $2.06 billion from $2.14 billion a year ago.
Revenue decreased slightly in the quarter because Seagate did not have enough manufacturing capacity to make a new line of high-end disk drives, said Don Waite, the company's chief financial officer.
Earnings came in better than expected, though, as Seagate combined some of its operations with that of Conner Peripherals Inc., a rival disk-drive maker Seagate bought last year.
"We've seen some significant cost reduction from that merger," Waite said.
Paul Weinstein, an analyst at PaineWebber in San Francisco, said Seagate had a good quarter but has a better outlook.

"Their inventories are down, their personal computer business is better, they've cleaned up the problems in their low-end market and as they ramp up the higher-end products, they should have a really good December quarter," Weinstein said.
